notes: Two defeaters conceded: the biconditional's necessity direction was induction from a small failure sample (WebPKI shows elements 3 and 5 substitutable by cheap exit), and bonded individual liability does not scale beyond the discretionary-judgment tier. Narrowed to sufficiency, with per-element necessity as separate conjectures and element 3 re-scoped to place liability wherever judgment is exercised.

Conceded rebutting defeater: bonded individual liability does not scale to high-volume automated assurance. Rescoped element 3 to "liability rests on whoever exercises judgment", bonding confined to the discretionary tier.

Conceded that the conditions were purely procedural. Condition 1 restated as an outcome test (assurance scores not predictable from wealth, age, digital participation beyond what evidence requires); element 4 extended to the substrate tier after the Estonia/ROCA test; scope limited explicitly to the structure of authority with a possible distributional condition left open.
